Note::TexAccessor::todos¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::todos() const

Extract \todo Note Bodies Per Source Cell¶

todos() extracts the required brace body from each \todo{...} command — a common convention (from packages such as todonotes) for leaving in-source review notes. It is useful for collecting outstanding authoring notes across a document independently of the surrounding text.

Unlike captions, the match here is a plain regular expression over a single, non-nested brace group — there is no starred form and no optional leading argument to skip. A body containing a nested brace group is not specially handled; the extractor’s group stops at the first unescaped }, the same boundary behavior as footnotes.

The closed TokenBatch stores every extracted note body in its rank-1 Text tokens() Note. Its Int64 offsets() has source.numel() + 1 entries, so flattened source cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). The receiver is not mutated.

Undefined yields undefined tokens with offsets [0]. Empty cells and cells without a \todo command produce empty intervals. Only Text is accepted.

Example 1: Multiple Notes In One Cell, And A Lone Note¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\todo{fix this} text \todo{and this too})",
    "no todos here",
    R"(\todo{lone})"});
const auto todos = source.tex().todos();

std::cout << todos.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["fix this", "and this too", "lone"]

Example 2: Per-Cell Offsets¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = todos.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 2, 3]

Cell 0 owns two notes, the plain-prose cell 1 owns none, and cell 2 owns its one note.

Example 3: No \todo Commands Anywhere¶

const auto empty_batch = pluss::make_note({"plain", ""}).tex().todos();
std::cout << empty_batch.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().todos().tokens().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().todos();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "todos Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
todos Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • warnings: extract compiler/package diagnostics instead of authoring notes.

  • footnotes: the same single-brace-group extraction pattern, for \footnote{...}.

  • captions: a semantic extractor with an optional leading argument to skip.
